title: Pure clutter promotes 165 ghost tracks
summary: A conventional M-of-N hit counter promotes tracks in a scene containing no targets because new-track covariance creates a gate large enough to consume random clutter.
trigger: Run 40 scans with zero targets and six false alarms per scan while confirming any tentative track that accumulates M hits in N scans.
observed: The historical implementation confirmed 165 tracks from pure clutter while producing plausible-looking trajectories.
invariant: Confirmation evidence must distinguish a concentrated target likelihood from an enormous gate that merely contains something.
fix: Replace hit counting with a Wald sequential test over a target-present versus clutter likelihood ratio.

timeline.title: Remove every real target
timeline.detail: Only a Poisson-like field of six false alarms per scan remains.

timeline.title: Let covariance inflate the gate
timeline.detail: Unknown velocity makes each tentative track accept almost any nearby clutter return.

timeline.title: Count the ghosts
timeline.detail: One hundred sixty-five false tracks reach confirmation in forty scans.

timeline.title: Score evidence quality
timeline.detail: The Wald score charges misses and rewards only concentrated likelihood under the target model.

limits: The clutter process and detection model are simulated; real sensor artifacts require a calibrated likelihood model.
